subject: chemistry
title: Diffusion
welcome_lead: Spray perfume in the corner and minutes later the whole room smells it. Why?
meta_desc: Understand diffusion in gases and liquids in this KS3 chemistry adventure.
final_note: You can now explain diffusion using particles.

concepts.def: Particles spreading from where they are crowded to where they are not.
Gas and liquid particles move in random directions.
How many particles are in a given space.
Particles diffuse from high to low concentration.
Diffusion of scent particles through the air.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Diffusion is the spreading out of particles. It happens because particles in gases and liquids are always moving in random directions.

Spread from crowded to empty.
You smell cookies baking across the kitchen — the smell particles diffuse through the air. A drop of ink in still water slowly spreads out through the liquid.

Diffusion is faster in gases than liquids because gas particles move faster and have more empty space.

It's also faster when the temperature is higher — particles have more energy.
